statement: Self-controlled, recite the chosen verse, the Raudrī or the Bahurūpī Gāyatrī; meditate on Oṃ and hold the fixation (dhāraṇā) in the heart (5.21-25).
for: Bringing yoga about: joining the mind to the Lord

statement: At the close of each chapter's observance he mutters its brahma-mantra: to Sadyojāta (1.39-44), to Vāmadeva and the others (2.21-27), to the non-terrible and terrible forms (3.20-26), to the Supreme Person (4.21-24), and to Īśāna (5.41-47).
for: The observance of each stage of the path
why_gap: What the five brahma-mantras do in the practice: the sūtras prescribe one at the end of each chapter but state no working.

for: Forgetfulness of the Lord; keeping the mind on Rudra

statement: Dwell in an empty house or a cave, constantly with the god, with senses conquered (5.9-11); through conquest of the senses one becomes unattached, constant in self and friendly (5.1-8).
for: Attachment and a scattered mind; becoming a yogin

statement: With his sign unmanifest and his conduct manifest, despised among all beings, he wanders being insulted (3.1-5), feigning snoring, trembling, limping, amorous gestures and senseless acts and speech so that he meets contempt (3.10-18).

warnings.text: Kauṇḍinya: the ascetic does this only once he has gained knowledge, his impurity is reduced and the teacher gives leave, and only by acts that do not conflict with the restraints (yama).

statement: Be joyful and not heedless; so one attains greatness in each and every observance (2.12-14).

Cut with the intellect the root of the net of causes of the faults, fix the whole mind on Rudra, and stay alone, secure, free from sorrow and vigilant; the end of sufferings then comes by the Lord's grace (5.35-40).

Powers are the sign that yoga has arisen: distant seeing, hearing, thinking and knowing, omniscience, swiftness of mind, taking forms at will (1.21-26); for one constantly yoked for six months they arise in abundance (5.12-13).
Practise austerity more, with devotion to none other than Śaṅkara, since the observance is the supreme gift, sacrifice and austerity (2.15-20).
Bathe with ash at the three junctures of the day (1.2) and lie in ash (1.3).
for: The first stage's purification: removal of impurity

rests_on.note: Kauṇḍinya 5.29: in the first stage bathing and the offerings are the action, removal of impurity the purification

statement: Attend on the Lord with the offering (upahāra) of laughter, song, dance, the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostration and muttering (1.8).

rests_on.note: Kauṇḍinya 5.29: bathing and laughter etc. are the first stage's action

statement: Keep the five restraints (non-harming, celibacy, truthfulness, non-dealing, non-stealing) and the five observances (non-anger, service of the teacher, purity, lightness of diet, vigilance) (1.9/2).
for: The ground of the observance; steadiness of conduct

statement: Give oneself (ātmapradāna) as the supreme gift; in giving, one also worships and performs austerity (2.18).
Be vigilant, as one guards a sprout, against heedlessness: inattention to what is to come, and dependence (5.39).
Endure the pairs of opposites, bodily, from beings and from the gods, as cows and deer do (5.18).
for: Being thrown about by heat and cold, praise and blame and the other pairs

statement: Approach the teacher seeking the end of suffering itself, not dharma, wealth, pleasure or isolation (1.1/7).
for: Choosing the aim with which to begin the path

statement: The second stage (going among people and courting contempt by feigned snoring, trembling, limping, signs of desire and senseless speech) is undertaken only after knowledge is gained, impurity reduced and with the teacher's leave, and only by acts that do not conflict with the restraints (3.12-17).
for: Taking up the practice of dishonour before one is fit

statement: The teacher takes a tested brahmin who has come from the householder or another āśrama, consecrates him with ash sanctified by the Sadyojāta and other mantras before the southern image of Mahādeva, and lets him hear the mantra (1.1/5).
for: Entering the path beyond the āśramas

rests_on.note: the teacher's activity in teaching is for grace (1.1/7)
